I been working this land forty years. My man passed some years back, my boy works in the city, sends money but the farm is mine. Fifteen mu is a lot for an old woman but I manage — hire the tractor for ploughing, hire help for garlic harvest. Let me think through this year, same as every year really.

**Wheat, 10 mu** — I plant when the cold comes in October. I buy the seed from the same dealer in town, the one my neighbor Old Wang uses. He gets good wheat so I follow him. I put two bags of the compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind — on each mu when I plough, that's one full bag and another half. Then in spring when the wheat wakes up I spread urea, about half a bag each mu. I water three times from the well — before winter, at jointing, and when the grain fills. I spray once for the yellow mites when I see them. Last year I got about 450 jin per mu, I hope same this year.

**Maize, 10 mu** — After wheat comes off in June I put maize straight in, no ploughing, just the seed drill. Hybrid seed, the one everyone around here uses. One bag compound at planting, then when it gets to my waist I side-dress urea, maybe half a bag per mu. Summer rain usually enough but I water once if July is dry. Spray once for the borer. Maize gives me maybe 550 jin a mu, it's reliable.

**Garlic, 5 mu** — This is my cash. Garlic eats a lot so I feed it a lot. Two bags compound per mu before planting in October, plus I spread chicken manure I buy from the chicken farm — one cart on each mu. In spring I topdress urea twice, total about one bag per mu. I water five times, garlic is thirsty. Spray two times for the rust and the maggot. Good year I get 1300 jin per mu, fresh weight. Garlic pays for everything.

I don't change much from last year. Changing is how you lose money.
